column2: ENGLISH
Princes of Darkness

The year 2010. While Vlad von Carstein raises Sylvania, the other lords of the night stir. Neferata rules her Silver Pinnacle, the Red Duke rides again from the north, and in the City of the Damned Merovech the Mad still sits his throne two centuries after the Red Pox. Choose a prince of darkness and claim the night.
the Damned
Knights of Irrana
Irranan
Host of the Black Knight
The Black Grail
A cup of black iron, cold to the touch, that never quite runs dry. What it holds smells of blood and tastes of wine. Those who drink from it dream of a lady in white whose face is a skull.
Cursed Mousillon

One of the dead rules Mousillon, and the duchy has gone back to what it was after the Red Pox. Sickness walks the streets, the taxes rot in the counting houses, and the dead march out to war beside the living.
The Red Pox
The Red Pox is loose in the streets. The carts go round every morning.
Quarantine
The gates are shut and the sick are walled in. Trade suffers, but the pox is kept out.
Flooded Quarter
The Grismerie is under water, and so is everything in it.
Chapel of the Grail Reconsecrated
The Chapel of the Grail is holy again. For now the Lady's light holds back the rot of Mousillon.
After the Festival of the Damned
The masks are off but the mob is not finished. Fires still burn in the lower city.
Blessed by Landuin
The ghost of Landuin saluted this knight at his tomb.
Shamed by Landuin
The ghost of Landuin turned away from this pilgrim, and the shame has settled in the bones.
Haunted by the Bride
A bride in grave-clothes waits at the foot of the bed every night.
Wed to the Dead
Married to the ghost bride of the Gardens of Sorrow. She whispers secrets in the dark, and she is jealous.
Pilgrimage to Landuin's Tomb
On the road to the Chapel of the Grail in Mousillon.
Visited Landuin's Tomb
Has made the pilgrimage to Landuin's tomb in the last twenty years.
The Dead of Mousillon
The dead of Mousillon have risen to fill the ranks.
Shared Merovech's Table
Fled the Feast
Tried to Poison Me
Rode on Mousillon
Betrayed the Black Knight
Pilgrimage to Landuin's Tomb

Ride to the ruined Chapel of the Grail in Mousillon and kneel at the tomb of Landuin, the greatest knight Bretonnia ever had. The worthy may be blessed. The unworthy will learn what they are. The road is dangerous, the city more so.
You drive the ghost back into its tomb.
You kill the thing in the water.
The Mad Duke sickens.

The plague carts are out in the lower city again. The pox-doctors say it is the Red Pox, the same sickness that killed half of Mousillon in 1813, and the people are already running to the river. The sick come out in red blotches, then they bleed from the eyes, then they die. In Mousillon they do not always stay dead.
Shut the gates and wall in the sick.
Let it burn itself out.
Let them die. They will rise again for me.

The gates held. Behind them the lower city screamed for a month and then went quiet, and when the masked men went in to burn the bodies the pox had burned itself out. Outside the walls, Mousillon lives.
The gates did not hold. Someone bribed a guard, or climbed the wall, or simply walked out through the sewers, and now the Red Pox is in the upper city too.
So be it.
The Red Pox has had its fill. The carts stop coming round and the pyres in the market square burn down to ash. Half the streets of the lower city are empty and the rats are fat.
The Red Pox has had its fill of the city, but not of you. You woke this morning with red marks on your arms and blood on your pillow.
Mousillon endures.

The Chapel of the Grail stands roofless in the rotten heart of Mousillon. The windows are gone and the floor is cracked by roots, but the tomb of Landuin is untouched. Not even the thieves of the city dare go near it. The stone knight on the lid holds his sword across his chest. The air is very cold.
Kneel at the tomb.

As you kneel, the cold goes out of the air. A knight in old armour is standing beside the tomb, pale as moonlight, and he lifts his sword to his face in salute. You feel stronger than you have in years. Then he is gone, and the chapel is only a ruin again.
I will be worthy of it.
You kneel and pray, and for a moment there is a knight standing beside the tomb, pale as moonlight. He looks at you for a long time. Then he turns his back. On the road home you cannot stop shaking.
He saw what I am.

Your foot is barely across the threshold when the lid of the tomb grinds aside. A knight of white light rises from it with his sword drawn, and the dead things that live in the chapel walls flee screaming. Landuin has come back to drive one more horror out of Mousillon.
Run!
I have killed better knights than you.
You kneel and pray at the tomb until your knees ache. Nothing happens. A crow watches from the broken window. If Landuin is here, he has nothing to say to you.
The road was the prayer.

A beggar catches your sleeve in the street. His face is hidden in a hood, and in his hands is a cup of black iron, full to the brim with something dark. "The Grail, my lord," he whispers. "The true Grail. Duke Maldred drank from it, and Merovech before him. Drink, and you will never be afraid again."
Give it to me.
Get away from me.
Cut him down and spill the cup.

Since you drank from the black cup you have had the same dream every night. A lady in white walks beside a lake, and when she turns to you her face is a skull. You wake hungry, and nothing in the kitchens will fill you.
What is she?

An old knight is kneeling in the ruins of the Chapel of the Grail. His surcoat is in rags and his armour is rusted, but there is a light around him that the rot of Mousillon cannot touch. He is a Grail Knight, one of the few who have drunk from the true Grail, and he has come to die where Landuin lies. He asks only that the chapel be made holy again.
I will pay for the work.
Let him die here, in peace.
This is no place for him. Send him away.
A Grail Knight. I have never tasted one.

The masons have finished and the bishop has sung the mass. For the first time in centuries, candles burn in the Chapel of the Grail. The old knight lay down before the altar on the last night of the work and did not get up again. He was smiling.

The work went badly from the first day. The stones wept blood, the masons fell sick, and the night before the bishop came, the new altar cracked from end to end. The old knight died the same night, and the men who found him would not say what his face looked like.
It is done.

The Grismerie is under water again. Every spring the river rises over the poorest quarter of Mousillon, and every spring the people on the roofs scream for boats that never come. This year the water is higher than anyone remembers. There is something big moving in it.
Bring the boats. I will lead them myself.
Wait for the water to go down.
Let them drown. The drowned make good servants.

You are pulling a child out of a window when the water heaves under your boat. Something vast and grey rises out of the flood, a mouth like a sewer lined with rings of teeth. The Dracoleech of the Grismerie is real, and it is hungry.
Steel, now!
Row! Row for your lives!

In the Gardens of Sorrow the Mousillon Rose grows over everything, and its pollen makes the air thick and sweet. Tonight there is a bride standing among the roses. Her dress is a shroud and her face is grey, and she has been waiting a very long time for a husband who never came. She says she will wait no longer. She looks at you.
Take [mousillon_groom.GetFirstName] instead.
Then I will marry you.
Fetch a priest!
Walk away and do not look back.
The priest prayed among the roses all night. At dawn the bride bowed her head, and when the sun touched her she was gone. The roses on that spot have since turned white.
The priest prayed among the roses all night. In the morning he was found sitting against the wall with his eyes gone and his mouth full of petals. The bride is still there, and now she is angry.
Lady help us.

You have been invited to dinner by Merovech, Duke of Mousillon, who fed his King to his court in 1813 and has not grown any saner since. The hall is hung with black and the guests do not look at each other. The meat is red and tender and the Duke watches you eat every bite. Nobody asks what it is.
Eat, and praise the cook.
Slip away before dessert.
Poison his cup.

You were seen. Before the Duke can even lift the cup his guards have you on the floor. Merovech laughs until he weeps blood, then has you dragged down to his dungeons. He says he will save you for a special occasion.
Lady preserve me.

[From.GetTitledFirstName] tried to poison your wine at the feast. The guards caught [From.GetObjectPronoun] before you drank, and [From.GetSubjectivePronoun] is now waiting in the dungeons for your pleasure.
Ungrateful guests.

It is the Festival of the Damned. The people of Mousillon are dancing in the streets in masks of skulls and rotting faces, and it is getting hard to tell the masks from the faces. The taverns are full. Some houses are already burning. The mob will go where it is pointed.
Let them have their festival.
Clear the streets. Use the cavalry.
Point them at [mousillon_rival.GetFirstName]'s house.

During the Festival of the Damned a masked mob broke into your house, smashed what they could not carry and set fire to the rest. Everyone knows who pointed them at your door: [From.GetTitledFirstName].
I will remember this.

Mousillon, the City of the Damned, is ruled by [mousillon_vampire.GetTitledFirstName], a thing that does not live. The dukes of Bretonnia say that it is a stain on the realm, and the Grail Knights say that the Lady wills it cleansed. The knights will ride if you call them.
For the Lady! We ride on Mousillon.
Mousillon is beyond saving.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has called the knights of Bretonnia to ride against you. They are coming down the old road under the Lady's banners, singing hymns. Mousillon has eaten crusades before.
Rise, my dead. Meet them.
Let them come.

A knight in black armour has come out of Mousillon with an army at his back. His name is Mallobaude, and he tells everyone who will listen that he is your son, the true heir of Bretonnia, cheated of his birthright by a father who did not want him. He says he will have his throne. Some of your knights are already listening.
He is no son of mine.
There was a woman, once...

A black knight called Mallobaude has raised his banner in Mousillon. Living knights who hate the King ride with him, and behind them walk the dead of the duchy. He wants Mousillon first, and then all of Bretonnia.
To arms!

A knight in black armour kneels before your throne. He is Mallobaude, bastard son of [mallo_king.GetTitledFirstName], and he wants his father's crown. He has knights who will follow him and hate enough for an army. What he lacks is an army that does not die. He offers you whatever you want, once he is king.
You will have your crown, my son.
Chain him and send him to his father.
I have a better use for royal blood.
A cart has come up from Mousillon under a flag of truce. In the back, in chains, is the black knight Mallobaude, who says he is your son. The lord of Mousillon sends him with compliments.
Take him below.

A herald in mouldering livery has come from Mousillon. He does not breathe. His masters, the Mousillonian Unliving, have heard that you are at war, and they will march for you, for gold. They want no food, no pay after the first and no rest, and when the war is over they will go back into the earth.
Here is your gold. March.
Go back to your grave.
